questions.question: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.note: Mercury is the only metallic element that is liquid at standard conditions; gallium and caesium melt just above room temperature.

questions.question: Which is the most abundant metal in the Earth's crust?
questions.note: Aluminium makes up about 8% of the Earth's crust, more than any other metal.

questions.question: Which metal has the highest electrical conductivity of all metals?
questions.note: Silver beats copper, which is the more common (and cheaper) conductor in wires.

questions.question: Bronze is traditionally an alloy of copper and which metal?
questions.note: Modern bronze is typically about 88% copper and 12% tin.

questions.question: Brass is an alloy of copper and which metal?
questions.note: The copper-to-zinc ratio is varied to get different colours and properties.

questions.question: When zinc reacts with dilute sulfuric acid, which gas is released?
questions.note: The acid strips zinc's protective layer and the reaction releases hydrogen gas.

questions.question: Which mineral is the main ore of iron?
questions.note: Hematite (Fe2O3) is the main ore of iron; bauxite is the ore of aluminium.

questions.question: Cast iron typically contains how much carbon?
questions.note: Cast iron has more than 2% carbon, which makes it hard but brittle; steel has less.

questions.question: Stainless steels contain a minimum of about how much chromium?
questions.note: At least about 10.5% chromium is needed to form the protective surface layer.

questions.question: In a blast furnace, what is the main role of coke?
questions.option_1: A flux that removes impurities from the melt
questions.option_2: A reducing agent for the iron ore
questions.option_4: A lining material for the furnace
questions.note: Coke (carbon) reduces the iron oxide to molten iron and also burns as fuel.

questions.question: In basic oxygen steelmaking, what is blown into molten pig iron to lower its carbon content?
questions.note: Pure oxygen blown through the melt burns off excess carbon, turning pig iron into steel.

questions.question: Wrought iron is best described as iron with what?
questions.note: Wrought iron has less than about 0.05% carbon plus fibrous slag, making it soft and easy to forge.

questions.question: The eutectoid temperature in the iron-carbon diagram is about?
questions.category: Inside steel: phases and heat treatment
questions.note: At 727 °C austenite of eutectoid composition transforms into pearlite.

questions.question: Pearlite has a lamellar structure made of alternating layers of?
questions.category: Inside steel: phases and heat treatment
questions.note: Pearlite is roughly 87% soft ferrite and 13% hard cementite in layers.

questions.question: The eutectoid composition of steel is about how much carbon?
questions.category: Inside steel: phases and heat treatment
questions.note: A steel with 0.76% carbon transforms entirely into pearlite at the eutectoid temperature.

questions.question: Martensite forms in carbon steels when austenite is?
questions.category: Inside steel: phases and heat treatment
questions.note: Quenching is so fast that carbon atoms cannot escape, trapping them in a hard, strained structure.

questions.question: Austenite (gamma iron) has which crystal structure?
questions.category: Inside steel: phases and heat treatment
questions.note: Above 912 °C iron switches from body-centered cubic to the face-centered cubic gamma form.

questions.question: Annealing is a heat treatment used mainly to?
questions.option_3: Add carbon to the surface by carburizing
questions.category: Inside steel: phases and heat treatment
questions.note: Annealing softens the metal and relieves internal stresses, making it more workable.

questions.question: In the Hall-Héroult process, alumina dissolved in molten cryolite is treated how to extract aluminium?
questions.note: Electric current through the molten bath deposits aluminium metal at the cathode.

questions.question: The Bayer process produces alumina from which ore?
questions.note: Bauxite is digested in hot caustic soda, leaving alumina that feeds the Hall-Héroult cells.

questions.question: The Kroll process is the main industrial method for producing which metal?
questions.note: Titanium tetrachloride is reduced with magnesium to give titanium sponge.

questions.question: Pure copper for electrical use is produced at the final stage by?
questions.note: Electrorefining deposits copper of about 99.99% purity at the cathode.

questions.question: Duralumin, one of the earliest age-hardenable alloys used in aircraft, is aluminium alloyed mainly with?
questions.note: Duralumin is a classic aluminium-copper alloy that gains strength as fine precipitates form.

questions.question: Galvanization protects steel or iron from rusting by coating it with?
questions.note: The zinc coating shields the steel and corrodes sacrificially in its place.

questions.question: The Charpy V-notch test measures what property of a material?
questions.note: A swinging pendulum breaks the notched sample; the energy it loses is the material's toughness.

questions.question: The ultimate tensile strength (UTS) is?
questions.option_1: The stress at which a material starts to deform permanently under load
questions.option_2: The stress at fracture under impact
questions.option_3: The maximum stress a material can withstand while being stretched
questions.option_4: The stress a material can bear forever
questions.note: UTS is the peak of the stress-strain curve, the highest load the material can take in tension.

questions.question: The Brinell hardness test presses what into the material's surface?
questions.note: A hard ball (usually tungsten carbide) is pushed in under a set load; the dent size gives the hardness.

questions.question: Fatigue failure in a material is caused by?
questions.note: Cracks start and grow under many load cycles, even at stresses below the ultimate strength.

questions.question: Creep is the tendency of a solid material to?
questions.option_1: Fracture suddenly without any applied load
questions.option_2: Deform slowly and permanently under stress
questions.note: Creep gets worse with time and temperature, which is why it matters in turbines and boilers.

questions.question: In a tensile test, ductility is commonly measured by?
questions.note: How much the sample stretches before breaking, in percent, tells how ductile it is.

questions.question: Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen in the presence of?
questions.note: Rust is a mix of iron oxides and hydroxides that needs both oxygen and moisture to form.

questions.question: Sacrificial anodes protecting ship hulls and pipelines are commonly made of?
questions.note: These metals are more active than steel, so they corrode first and spare the structure.

questions.question: TIG (tungsten inert gas) welding uses which kind of electrode?
questions.note: The tungsten electrode does not melt; an inert gas shields the arc and the weld pool.

questions.question: Traditional solder used to join electronic components is a fusible alloy of?
questions.note: Classic solder melts at low temperature to bond metal parts without melting them.

questions.question: Carburizing hardens the surface of steel by making it absorb which element while heated?
questions.note: Heating steel in a carbon-rich medium diffuses carbon into the surface so it can be hardened.

questions.question: In galvanic corrosion of two different metals in contact, which metal corrodes preferentially?
questions.note: The more active metal becomes the anode of the galvanic cell and corrodes first.

questions.question: The iron pillar of Delhi is famous for what?
questions.category: Metallurgy in India and modern materials
questions.note: A protective film on its high-phosphorus iron has kept it nearly rust-free for centuries.

questions.question: Wootz steel, a high-carbon crucible steel once famous worldwide, originated in?
questions.category: Metallurgy in India and modern materials
questions.note: Wootz steel was made in ancient India from the mid-1st millennium BC and traded widely.

questions.question: Which country produced more than half of the world's steel in 2023?
questions.category: Metallurgy in India and modern materials
questions.note: China accounted for about 54% of world steel production in 2023.

questions.question: Nickel-based superalloys are the material of choice for which high-temperature application?
questions.option_2: Gas turbine blades in jet engines
questions.category: Metallurgy in India and modern materials
questions.note: They keep their strength near their melting point, ideal for hot turbine sections.

questions.question: Nitinol, the shape-memory alloy, is made of nickel and which other metal in roughly equal atomic percentages?
questions.category: Metallurgy in India and modern materials
questions.note: Nickel-titanium 'remembers' its shape and springs back when warmed.

questions.question: Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) was established in 1907 in which city?
questions.category: Metallurgy in India and modern materials
questions.note: The company was established on 26 August 1907 in Jamshedpur.
